reason: Regulators allowing telemarketers' prerecorded "robo calls" is an industry-regulation story that fits Business or World about as well as telecoms Sci/Tech.
"Olympics day four ... going for gold for Great Britain" is a live Olympics report, plainly Sports.
"A final test is likely to confirm a second U.S. case of mad cow disease" is a disease-testing story; nothing in the text is about markets or trade.
"The Times of London has gone strictly tabloid ... compact format" is newspaper company news, not science or technology.
"tightening of security at all Olympic venues" is an Olympics story (Sports) but the intruder/security angle is equally defensible as World.
A reality "series about infidelity" is entertainment/human interest (World), though the "online matchmaking service" premise gives Sci/Tech a foothold.
OPM, "which sets hiring and employment standards for the government", reviewing employees is a government story, not Sci/Tech.
"A Georgia school board is in court" over evolution stickers is a court case (World) about a science topic (Sci/Tech); both are defensible.
"how footballers should prepare themselves for the high-pressure penalties" is a football story, and anything sports is Sports.
"Christmas spirit is a bargain-hunting essential" barely supports any section; shopping leans Business but the text cannot really be classified from its own words.
"the world's fastest computer - a 16,000-processor version of its BlueGene/L supercomputer" is hardware news, Sci/Tech.
"Bakery cafe chain Panera Bread Co. hopes its customers will stick around" to boost sales is company news; the "try the Wi-Fi" mention is incidental.
A Hollywood producer's "latest gig, as a satellite radio talk-show host" is celebrity/human interest (World), with satellite radio as a weak Sci/Tech hook.
Google warning that "fiercer competition is set to hit sales growth" after its "share flotation" is a tech company's purely financial story.
"beat Victor Hanescu of Romania 6-4, 6-4 ... in the first round of the Open de Moselle" is a tennis result, Sports.
"Unisys Corp. plans to cut 1,400 jobs" is a tech company's labour/financial story with no technology content, so Business and Sci/Tech both fit.
"a clinical trial found it doubled the risk of heart attack and stroke" is medicine, but "withdrawn from sale" makes the product-recall Business reading defensible.
"Republican-dominated election board met behind closed doors" over ousting an elections administrator is politics, World.
"Shareholders approved ... sale of one of its two remaining operating divisions" turning the firm "into a mortgage investment fund" is clearly Business.
IRS "income tax refund checks could not be delivered" is personal-finance/tax news (Business) but equally a government/human-interest item (World).
"2 charged after Chicago area pals are slain" is a crime story, World, with no sports content.
"The International Cricket Council are to open a global cricket academy" is cricket governance, Sports.
"Red Hat replaces CFO" amid "restating its earnings" is a tech company's purely financial story.
"Letters. The postbag, and your miscellaneous musings" cannot be classified from its own words; the "FUD" jargon only weakly suggests a tech letters column.
"South African skipper Graeme Smith" on "an upcoming two-Test series against India" is cricket, Sports.
"Vodafone hires Citi for Cesky bid" is a deal-advisory story about a telecom, fitting Business deals and Sci/Tech tech-industry deals equally.
"a plan to raise 200m to block a takeover of Man Utd" is sports business (Sports by convention) but the Nomura financing angle makes Business defensible.
"The Nikkei average rose 1.37 percent at the opening" is a market report, Business.
"A wandering Congress trips over the US Constitution" is politics, World, with no business content.
Microsoft settling "antitrust lawsuits with Novell" is a tech-industry lawsuit (Sci/Tech by convention) but also plain company news (Business).
"House Passes Corporate Tax Bill" with "breaks to manufacturing companies" is both congressional politics (World) and business/tax news (Business).
"Google Inc. stock dropped more than 6 percent" as lock-up shares hit the market is a tech company's purely financial story.
"The state's Adult Protective Services agency will get an emergency infusion of $10 million" is state government news, World.
"my struggle to remain a vegetarian ... while travelling" is a personal human-interest column with no science or technology content.
"Some women with breast cancer are less likely to have their tumours picked up by scans" is medicine, Sci/Tech.
"U.S. Softball Team Wins ... 5-0 over Australia, putting them into the gold medal game" is Sports.
"Australia were 362 for seven wickets at the close of play" in a cricket test is Sports.
Using "Craigslist to furnish her ... apartment" and asking "fellow Craigslisters" is an internet story, but the headline frames it as a company-in-a-city piece, so Business is defensible.
Israel "liquidating the Erez industrial zone" before "the first stage of the disengagement plan" is Middle East politics, World.
"Companies across the country are offering yoga and meditation classes" to employees is workplace/company news, not Sci/Tech.
"reported a 41 percent rise in quarterly profit ... beating Wall Street forecasts" is an earnings story for a defense contractor, Business.

"Greek weightlifter Leonidas Sampanis will find out ... if he is to be stripped of his medal" is Sports.
"Undergraduates in the city earn more than 90 a week on average" is a student-earnings survey that reads as Business or human-interest World.
"a big first-day jump in shares of Google" and its IPO "auction" is a tech company's purely financial story.
"The Japanese information services industry clocked up sales of 13,703.9 billion yen" is an industry sales report, Business (or Sci/Tech), not World.
"The United States and its major economic allies struggled ... to relieve the heavy debt burden for Iraq" is international diplomacy (World) about debt/finance (Business).
"The Ontario government plans to introduce legislation" on school leaving age is government/education news, World.
"Pakistan take a slim lead over Sri Lanka ... in the first Test" is cricket, Sports.

"Rumors Suggest Photo Ability To Be Added to iPod" is a consumer-hardware product story, Sci/Tech.
"Donors to the Palestinians are asking whether the change of leadership" will open up finances is political/aid diplomacy (World) about public finances (Business).
Whether "Verizon ... snap up a luxury suite at the $440 million ballpark" is corporate spending (Business) or sports business (Sports).

"the next version of its enterprise instant messaging software" is a software release, Sci/Tech.
"the Indianapolis Colts shredded the New England Patriots for a 17-13 halftime lead" is Sports.

"PeopleSoft revises third-quarter profit" after a severance "tax adjustment" is a tech company's purely financial story.

"Avaya ... agreeing to acquire German enterprise communications vendor Tenovis" is a tech-industry deal (Sci/Tech by convention) and an acquisition (Business).
"Tim Henman won his opening match at the Swiss Indoors tennis tournament" is Sports.
"the release to manufacturing of Microsoft Operations Manager (MOM) 2005" is a software release, Sci/Tech.
"considering more tax cuts" amid "the 9.1 billion dollar budget surplus" is fiscal policy that fits Business or government World.
"Infineon will plead guilty to price fixing of DRAM chips and will pay $160 million in fines" is a corporate-crime story (Business) in the chip industry (Sci/Tech).
"Virginia's 10-year experiment with red-light cameras ... expires next year" is a state policy-renewal question (World) about a technology (Sci/Tech).
"Gazprom is an instrument of public administration just like the pro-Kremlin United Russia" is political analysis of a company, defensible as World or Business.
"Tokyo stocks rose moderately Monday morning on bargain hunting" is a market report, Business.
"TheStreet.com Inc. ... may be up for sale ... sparking a 7 percent rise in its shares" is a company-sale story; being a "Web site" is incidental.

"sending the Nasdaq composite index up 1.6 percent ahead of Google Inc.'s ... initial public offering" is a market report, Business.

"Scotch Whisky eyes Asian and Eastern European markets" is an industry/trade story, Business.
"Stock of Google Inc. powered to new highs" on "strong financial results" is a tech company's purely financial story.
"stocks edging higher" as "the price of crude declined" is a Wall Street market report, Business.
"Saturday's final of the triangular cricket tournament" threatened by rain is Sports.
"Jackie Stewart rejects Bernie Ecclestone's claims that the British Grand Prix is dead" is Formula One, Sports.
"Rich countries are giving only half the amount they promised ... the UN says" is international aid politics, World, not science.
"Hynix Semiconductor ... third-quarter net profit more than tripled" is an earnings story (Business, or at most Sci/Tech), certainly not World.

"Governor Mitt Romney is calling for the resignation of the head of the state's Turnpike Authority" is state politics, World.

"Producer prices surged 1.7 percent in October" fuelling "Inflation Fears" is economics, Business.

"Heart patients aren't more likely to live long term after getting ... stents, according to a study" is medicine, Sci/Tech.
"Va. GOP members chose Del. Thelma Drake ... to replace Rep. Edward L. Schrock" is politics, though the headline "Prove Powerful on Web" frames the internet as the story.
"one of the toughest endurance sports around: the deca-ironman" with a "world record" is Sports.
